title: URL SHORTENER (BITLY)
subtitle: It sounds like a toy, but it is the cleanest example of a read-heavy system: almost every request is a redirect.
footer: DDIA: Ch 5 replicas · Ch 6 hash sharding   ·   Similar: Rate limiter · Business discovery · News feed · News aggregator

items: Redirects outnumber new links about 100 to 1, so the design is mostly about serving reads fast.
Generate short codes from a counter encoded in base62: unique by construction, no collision checks.
Put a cache in front of the database; a small share of links gets most clicks, so the hit rate is high.
Create a short URL for a long URL (optional custom alias, expiry)
Redirect short URL → original URL
Redirect p99 < 100ms
99.99% available for redirects
Short codes globally unique
Read:write ≈ 100:1
100M DAU × 10 clicks = 1B redirects/day ≈ 12k/s avg, ~100k/s peak.
Writes ~1M/day ≈ 12/s.
1B URLs × 500B = 500GB, which fits one Postgres.

Start simple: a write service creates a code and stores it in Postgres. ~12 writes/sec is nothing.
Redirects are 100× more frequent. 100k reads/sec straight to Postgres is what breaks first.

items: Redirects are 100× more frequent. 100k reads/sec straight to Postgres is what breaks first.
Add a Redis cache (code → URL). Clicks follow Pareto, so 80%+ hit the cache in under 1ms. Postgres only sees misses; add replicas if needed.
Generate codes from a global counter: Redis INCR + base62. 7 chars = 3.5 trillion codes, no collisions. Servers grab IDs in batches of 1,000.
How do you guarantee unique codes?
Counter + base62 is unique by construction. Hashing (MD5 prefix) needs a unique constraint plus retry on collision.
302: every click reaches you (analytics, expiry, editing). 301 lets browsers cache it, which cuts load but loses analytics.
What if the counter node dies?
Redis with AOF + replica, or servers lease ranges from a Postgres sequence. A crash wastes a range; gaps are harmless.
Custom aliases?
Same table with a unique constraint; the insert fails if taken. Keep namespaces apart (e.g., counter codes are 7 chars, aliases ≥ 8).
Sharding 500GB at 12 writes/sec. It fits one machine; scale reads with cache and replicas.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
